title: Hybrid Monte Carlo for the extended Kane-Mele-Hubbard model
authors: Finn L. Temmen, Thomas Luu, Johann Ostmeyer, Lin Wang
abstract: The Hubbard model offers a powerful minimal description of strongly correlated electrons in molecules and materials, yet it neglects effects observed in nature that give rise to a much richer variety of physics. For instance, including nonlocal interactions introduces a competition between strongly correlated phases, while incorporating spin-orbit coupling (SOC) can lead to the emergence of exotic topological phases. Seeking a more realistic platform for simulating graphene and, potentially, related materials such as transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), we therefore consider the extended Kane-Mele-Hubbard model, which features a Kane-Mele SOC term and nearest-neighbor interactions. Simulating this model is particularly challenging once the nonlocal interactions become dominant over the on-site Hubbard interaction, as a severe sign problem arises already at half filling, leaving this regime largely unexplored. In this work, we develop continuous auxiliary field formulations of the model, suitable for treatment with the Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) algorithm. Using these formulations, we characterize the sign problem across the model's parameter space and establish where simulations are feasible, as a first step toward the full phase diagram.
summary: This paper tackles the computational challenge of simulating the extended Kane-Mele-Hubbard model, a realistic platform for studying topological materials. The authors develop a path integral formulation solvable by the Hybrid Monte Carlo algorithm. By analyzing the sign problem across various interaction regimes, they map out the parameter space where accurate quantum simulations are feasible.
main_problem: The primary challenge is simulating the extended Kane-Mele-Hubbard model when nonlocal interactions dominate, as this regime suffers from a severe sign problem.
main_result: The authors successfully developed a path integral formulation suitable for HMC, characterizing the sign problem across the parameter space and finding that the sign problem is mild at half filling.
method: The study uses the Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) algorithm applied to a path integral representation derived via the Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation and Suzuki-Trotter decomposition.
model_or_system: The system is the extended Kane-Mele-Hubbard model on a 2D honeycomb lattice, incorporating nearest-neighbor hopping, on-site interaction (U), nearest-neighbor interaction (V), and Kane-Mele Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC).
key_observables: The average phase $\Sigma$ is used to quantify the severity of the sign problem across the parameter space.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the ratio of nonlocal to on-site interactions ($K_V/U$), the SOC strength ($\lambda_{SO}$), and the chemical potential ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The methodology relies on the Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation and a second-order Suzuki-Trotter decomposition, which introduces an $O(\Delta t^2)$ error.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the sign problem diagnostic ($\Sigma$) as a function of varying $V$, $U$, and $\mu$, showing how the sign problem deepens when nonlocal interactions become dominant relative to on-site interactions.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the model and the difficulty posed by the sign problem. It then details the theoretical machinery: applying the Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation and deriving the path integral representation suitable for HMC simulation. Finally, it presents systematic scans over model parameters to map the feasibility of the simulation.
why_interesting: The development of robust numerical techniques (HMC on auxiliary field formulations) to tackle the sign problem in complex topological models like Kane-Mele systems is highly relevant for understanding strongly correlated topological phases.
